claims.statement: The shift window equals formal shift start plus working hours plus a fixed 30-min handover tail (交班尾): day-shift ends are uniformly 16:30 (11h 05:00–16:30, 10h 06:00–16:30, 8h 08:00–16:30) and the mid shift starts 16:30 with window ends 04:00/03:00/01:00 next day for 11h/10h/8h. The window end is the sole computation caliber for counting, target splitting and display, while the point where working hours are finished (03:30/02:30/00:30) is only a physical off-duty annotation; the 2026-09-23 decision rests on the measurement that 0 vehicles exit during the 30-min tail (08-24~09-22) and that the window-end cut is drift-resistant. Caliber sources: BM note 2026-09-19, README 关键口径 班次窗口与窗末 row, docs/08 §二·1.

Attribution windows differ from working windows: the day-shift attribution window is [04:45, 16:30] — early work 04:45–formal start counts as the day shift — while the mid-shift attribution window is [16:30, window end] (attr_start = 16:30 exactly), and the gap (mid window end, 04:45) has no attribution (a low-trough micro-gap). Consumers apply attr_start <= t < end semantics (dashboard active_shifts_at over current + previous day, so a midnight hour belongs to the previous day's mid shift), and causal history builders drop exit events in 04:45–16:30 for the same reason.

shifts.Shift is a frozen dataclass carrying kind ('day'|'mid'), nominal day (mid shift's day = opening day), work_start (anchor origin), attr_start (exit-counting origin), end (the window end used by the 't + remaining ≤ shift end' completion rule), and type. shift_windows(day, day_type, mid_type, schedule) returns [day?, mid?] with None types producing no shift (both None → []), and when a schedule dict is passed and contains the day, the schedule entry (values routed through normalize_shift_type, so 11/'10'/'休' all work) takes precedence over the positional day_type/mid_type arguments, yielding [] on rest days.

Each shift exposes a multi-anchor set work_start+{3,4,5,6}h (anchors/ANCHOR_HOURS) and a gate anchor at work_start+5h (gate_anchor, GATE_ANCHOR_H=5): day 11h→10:00, day 10h→11:00, day 8h→13:00, and the mid-shift gate anchor is always 21:30 regardless of 8/10/11h. Replay consumers (spike_w2/02_replay_shift, spike_w3/02_shadow_replay) iterate shift_windows + anchors per shift, and the W3 5-minute frame context (dashboard.build_frame_ctx) uses the same work_start+{3,4,5,6}h anchor set.

detect_day_type self-learns the day-shift type from 15-minute event buckets at 05:00/06:00/08:00: it returns None when the day has fewer than MIN_DAY_EVENTS=500 events (shutdown day); otherwise the earliest bucket with count ≥ SURGE_MIN_15MIN=30 determines the type (05:00→11h, 06:00→10h, 08:00→8h) — the threshold 30 sits between the measured low-trough floor (~12% of peak ≈ 7–8 events/15min) and full takt (~40–60) — and if no bucket reaches the threshold (gradual ramp) it falls back to the most common type '10h', recorded in the replay audit table.

detect_mid_type self-learns the mid-shift type from the minutes (last_min) between D 16:30 and the last product-vehicle exit event in the mid segment [D 16:30, D+1 04:45): None (no events) or < MID_MIN_FLOOR=300 (real 8h mid ends ≈480–540min, so <300min signals data truncation) → None; ≥630 → 11h; ≥510 → 10h; otherwise 8h. A 10h type whose furnace-side tail trails past 03:00 can be misjudged as 11h, which is why the raw value is preserved in the audit table.

Type self-learning (detect_day_type/detect_mid_type) uses full-day events including post-anchor events and is explicitly replay-hindsight caliber: the shifts.py header marks it 【回放专用】 and states production (W3) must not reuse it directly. The online causal path in spike_w3/plan_loader.py is a separate re-implementation banned from importing detect_*, enforced by a source-discipline test; meanwhile the historical-learning consumer spike_w3/predictor.build_takt_baseline legitimately applies the W2 detectors over pure past windows (rolling 8-week range, no future leakage).

normalize_shift_type implements the minimal business input vocabulary for the shift-calendar interface: it maps 11/10/8, '11', '10h', '8h' to '11h'/'10h'/'8h' and 休/休息/0/blank/None to None (rest/shutdown). Per the README 排班日历接口 row (W2.1 极简设计), business staff only enter 8/10/11/休 and the system maps hours to physical windows automatically; the plan table is used only during prediction/alert phases, with 0% dependency in the training phase.

resolve_shift(d, plan, history) is the frozen-contract (docs/02) production type orchestrator: a plan row for d yields (day_h, mid_h, 'plan'); a missing day falls through to infer_shift_causal(history, d.weekday()) yielding source 'inferred'. WeeklyPlan.shift_windows(d) is a static-plan convenience that must not be looped directly on the online path because a missing day and a both-sides-rest day both return [], and a raw loop would silently bypass the fallback.

infer_shift_causal(history, weekday) is a pure function (no DB) for the no-plan fallback: it filters history to the same weekday and takes the per-side mode, where rest (None) does not enter side voting, ties resolve to the newer day's value, missing samples default to (11, 11, 'inferred'), a side with no non-rest samples defaults to 11h, and samples that are all-rest on both sides yield (None, None, 'inferred').

recent_shift_history(conn, now, weeks=2) builds the causal 14-day sample of completed days [(date, day_h|None, mid_h|None)]: it sets SET TIME ZONE 'Asia/Shanghai', clamps the sample upper bound to min(now.date()-1, max DATE_EVT date) so the current (unclosed) day and days beyond observed data are excluded rather than treated as rest, reads only events with DATE_EVT < now (causal red line) for product vehicles (BODY_ID LIKE '78202%') and the 4 exit stations, and attributes exit events < 04:45 to the previous day's mid segment.

classify_completed_day(day_evts, mid_exit_evts) re-implements the W2 heuristics inline for completed days only: day type via the same 15-min bucket test (reusing shifts.SURGE_MIN_15MIN/MIN_DAY_EVENTS constants, no-hit ramp → 10h) and mid type via the last exit's minutes-from-16:30 with the same ≥630→11, ≥510→10, else 8 thresholds and < MID_MIN_FLOOR(300) → None (truncation); zero exits and zero events on both sides mean a rest day (None, None). It deliberately does not import the W2 detect_* functions (replay-hindsight semantics).

Weekly plan input follows a fixed spec (docs/08, finalized 2026-09-22): 6 columns 日期,日班工时,中班工时,出车计划,进车计划,备注 with the first 4 required (missing core header → table-level failure); dates accept YYYY-MM-DD or M/D; hours accept 8/10/11 with 休/0/blank meaning rest; 出车计划 is the all-day exit target (0 on rest days) and 进车计划/备注 are optional. Files go into the watch folder plan_inbox/ (dev default, overridable via the .env key DSS_PLAN_FOLDER / DSSConfig.plan_folder) named week_plan_<year>KW<ISO-week>*, with extensions .csv/.xlsx/.xls matching the name regex.

The parser (parse_csv/parse_excel sharing _rows_from_grid) is row-tolerant: CSV is decoded as utf-8-sig (BOM optional), Excel reads the first sheet with openpyxl data_only, header cells are stripped before matching, and bad rows (unparseable dates, illegal hours like 12, non-integer totals like 920.5 while integral floats 920.0 are accepted) are skipped and recorded in bad_rows without crashing or defaulting; duplicate dates within a file → last row wins plus a trace; empty files produce one trace entry. M/D dates are resolved by trying candidate years file_year ± 1 and picking the one whose ISO (year, week) matches the filename (year, KW) — no match or a date outside the file's ISO week makes the row a true bad row.

load_plan(folder) scans the directory (files not matching the week_plan name regex are silently ignored), records a sha256 hash for every recognized file, and merges rows across files: same date with identical (day_h, mid_h, total, entry) values merges (later file in lexicographic order owns source_file) while different values raise ValueError pre-insertion. Table-level ParseError, corrupted files, and unsupported .xls (recognized but recorded, re-save as .xlsx/CSV) are all traced without crashing — startup robustness requires that any bad file in plan_inbox must not drag down the online main loop.

WeeklyPlan accessors: plan_target(d) returns (day_target, mid_target) via alert_engine.split_target (single source of truth, F10) using the docs/08 formula day share = H_day/(H_day+H_mid) with largest-remainder rounding (11+11 → 50:50, 11+10 → ~52.4:47.6), and a missing row or None total returns (None, None) — plan targets are never guessed (2026-09-27 user decision ③). rest_days() yields days with both shifts rest (B3 expected-silence), and missing(d0, d1) lists uncovered dates in a closed interval for coverage checks.

persist_plan(conn, plan) upserts into dss.dim_weekly_plan (PK plan_date, ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) and dss.work_plan_file_meta (PK file_name + sha256) idempotently: per file it first compares the stored sha256 — identical content skips all writes, changed or new files upsert only their own rows, renamed files overwrite the rows they previously wrote, and no DELETE is ever issued; all writes run in one transaction, and failure rolls back preserving old data (shadow discipline). ensure_weekly_plan_tables lazily creates both tables and must run before check_dim_tables in boot_sequence (L3).

01_boot_online.load_week_plan is the boot entrypoint: DSS_PLAN_CSV env selects single-file mode (replay dry-run override, legacy behavior); otherwise load_plan(cfg.plan_folder) runs, with ValueError (cross-file conflict) or no/empty files returning None. None triggers the fallback self-learn mode ('兜底自学模式：班制推断、无目标') per docs/08 容错安全网 — the service never stops because of a missing plan, shift types come from causal inference and plan targets simply do not exist; plan_note_text renders the three states (fallback / loaded n days m files / missing-day + bad-row annotations), replay_rest_days reuses the same load for the B3 expected-silence set, and boot_sequence persists the plan with failure reported as a warning without aborting.

Shift-window constants exist only in spike_w2/shifts.py: spike_w3/common.py re-exports the whole shifts module (CST, DAY_TYPES, MID_END_TIMES, Shift, shift_windows, anchors, gate_anchor, is_complete, …) and copying window constants into W3 is a forbidden global constraint (B1); tests assert window values against the shifts constants to prevent copied-value drift. is_complete(shift, replay_start, replay_end) = attribution window ⊆ replay window (rule C2), excluding incomplete shifts from the door-judgment list and acting as a safety net in replay since the day loop starts at the first replay day. All shift/time logic is Asia/Shanghai-based (CST = ZoneInfo('Asia/Shanghai'); factory time = UTC+8, session default UTC).
